questions.question: In an optimization model, what does the objective function do?
options: It lists the decision vectors the model allows
It states a requirement each decision must meet
It returns the best decision vector of the model
It gives each decision vector a numerical value

questions.question: A model minimizes total transport cost. Plan A has cost 540 and plan B has cost 510; both are allowed. Which statement about moving from A to B is correct?
options: It is a worsening, since the objective value has dropped
It is an improvement only if B also ships more goods
It is neither, since only the optimal plan matters
It is an improvement, since a lower cost is better here

questions.question: A model chooses $\boldsymbol{x}=(x_1,x_2,x_3)$, and its objective is total profit $z$. What kind of object is the objective value $z$ of a plan?
options: A vector, such as $(10,0,4)$
A set of plans with equal profit
One number, such as 840 euros
An inequality such as $z\le840$

questions.question: A factory uses as its objective the total revenue of its products, to be made as large as possible. Why is this objective usually flawed for choosing a production plan?
options: It ignores costs, so it may favour products that earn little
Nothing is flawed, since revenue and profit rank plans alike
Costs belong in the constraints, so the objective is complete
Revenue cannot be written as a function of the decisions

questions.question: In the objective $z=c_1x_1+\cdots+c_nx_n$, where the $x_j$ are decision variables and the $c_j$ given numbers, what does $c_2$ represent?
options: The value of $x_2$ in the best plan
The total contribution of $x_2$ to $z$
The largest value $x_2$ is allowed to take
The change in $z$ per extra unit of $x_2$

questions.question: For the objective $z=4x_1+3x_2$, what is the objective value of the plan $(x_1,x_2)=(5,2)$?
A model minimizes $z=2x_1+5x_2$, where $x_1,x_2$ are units of two products. Four allowed plans are compared. Which has the best objective value?

Goods are sent by route 1 at 7 euros per tonne and by route 2 at 4 euros per tonne; $y_1,y_2$ are the tonnes sent on each route. Total transport cost is to be as small as possible. Which objective states this?

A workshop pays a fixed rent of 1000 euros per month, whatever it produces. Its profit objective is (revenue minus variable costs) minus 1000. How does the rent affect the best allowed production plan?
options: Not at all; it lowers every plan's profit by the same 1000
It moves the best plan towards producing more, to cover the rent
It moves the best plan towards producing less, to save costs
It changes the best plan, since every cost must be weighed

questions.question: In a profit model, plan A earns 500 but exceeds a capacity limit, while plan B earns 450 and satisfies all constraints. Which plan does the model's objective prefer, and why?
options: A, since its objective value is the higher one
B, as the objective compares only allowed plans
A, if its capacity overrun is small enough
A, as constraints are checked only after ranking by value

questions.question: For the objective $z=3x_1+2x_2$, the plans $(2,3)$ and $(4,0)$ both give $z=12$. What does this show?
options: The two plans must in fact be one and the same plan
Different plans can share one objective value
Both plans must be best plans for this model
The objective must have been computed wrongly

questions.question: Chairs sell for 50 and use 20 of material and 2 labour hours; tables sell for 120 and use 45 of material and 5 labour hours. Labour costs 8 per hour. With $x_1$ chairs and $x_2$ tables, what is the profit objective?
Flour sells for 2.40 euros per kg. A model defines $x$ as the flour sold in units of 100 kg and writes revenue as $c\,x$ euros. What must $c$ be?
For a production model choosing $x_1,x_2$, an analyst proposes as objective the total market demand for the two products, a number fixed by the market. Why is this not a useful objective?
options: Nothing is wrong, as demand is what the firm wants to meet
It should be made as large as possible, not as small
It gives every plan the same value, so it cannot rank them
It is useful once a demand constraint is also added

questions.question: A firm considers maximizing profit per unit produced instead of total profit. Why do these two objectives generally select different plans?
options: They are the same objective, measured in different units
Per-unit profit always gives more total profit as well
Per-unit profit differs from total profit only by a constant
Per-unit profit can favour making very few high-margin units

questions.question: A product sells for 9 per unit and needs 2 of labour per unit made. Each unit also uses one part bought last month for 5; unused parts cannot be returned or used elsewhere. What coefficient should the product get in the profit objective for this month's plan?
options: 2 per unit
7 per unit
9 per unit
4 per unit

questions.question: A model minimizes $z=4x_1-3x_2$ subject to $0\le x_1\le5$ and $0\le x_2\le5$. Which plan is best?
